In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions and their connection with QCD phase structure.
the question whether a pion lattice forms at chemical freezeout in heavy-ion collisions and, if so, what the implications are for the nature of the QCD equation of state.
the study of the properties of the hot, dense matter created in heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QGP has not been produced yet in the SPS collisions.
there are no indications for a phase transition in the SPS data, although there may well have been some indications for a phase boundary.
the data are compatible with a scenario where the pions are produced in a locally equilibrating system, but that the data are not conclusive enough to rule out other possibilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method to probe the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and have found evidence of a possible pion lattice at the SPS energy.
we have developed a new tool to probe the small length scales in the early stage of heavy-ion collisions.
the event-by-event fluctuation analysis is very powerful in probing the small length scales and the local properties in heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful analysis of the two-particle distribution in heavy-ion collisions may provide a unique probe of the prehadronic state of matter.
event-by-event correlation studies may provide the most direct probe of the QCD transition in heavy-ion collisions.
the QGP phase transition may be detectable by event-by-event fluctuations in the transverse momentum of particles in the final state.
